title_en: Aaron's rod transforms into a serpent
description_en: Aaron throws his rod before Pharaoh and it becomes a serpent. Egyptian magicians replicate it, but Aaron's serpent swallows theirs.
research_notes: Physical transformation of object. Egyptian magicians replicate — dual-source anomaly.

title_en: First plague: Nile turned to blood
description_en: Moses strikes the Nile; water turns to blood. Fish die, water stinks, Egyptians cannot drink. Lasts seven days.
research_notes: Mass environmental transformation. Affects all water in Egypt.

title_en: Second plague: frogs cover the land of Egypt
description_en: Frogs swarm out of the Nile and cover Egypt. At Moses's word, the frogs die and pile up in heaps.
research_notes: Sudden mass animal behaviour; reversed on command.

title_en: Third plague: lice/gnats from the dust
description_en: Aaron strikes the dust and lice (gnats) cover all humans and animals in Egypt. Egyptian magicians fail to replicate: 'this is the finger of God'.
research_notes: Magicians explicitly unable to replicate — their own diagnosis: divine intervention.

title_en: Fourth plague: swarms of flies, Goshen exempt
description_en: Dense swarms of flies cover Egypt. The land of Goshen (Israelite territory) is explicitly exempted — a geographic selectivity anomaly.
research_notes: Precision targeting: Goshen exempt. This geographic selectivity is a key UAP-relevance marker — not random natural phenomenon.

title_en: Fifth plague: disease kills Egyptian livestock, Israelite livestock unaffected
description_en: A severe disease kills all Egyptian livestock. Israelite livestock survive — again geographically selective.
research_notes: Precision selectivity: affects only Egyptian animals. Pharaoh confirms no Israelite animal died (v.7).

title_en: Sixth plague: boils on humans and animals
description_en: Moses throws soot into the air and it becomes festering boils on all Egyptians and animals. The magicians cannot stand before Moses because of the boils.
research_notes: Physical effect on human bodies triggered by airborne dispersal of material.

title_en: Seventh plague: hail and fire run together
description_en: YHWH sends the worst hailstorm in Egypt's history. Fire and hail run together (a physically anomalous combination). Again, Goshen is spared.
research_notes: Anomalous fire+hail combination defies normal physics. Goshen again exempt — targeted phenomenon.

title_en: Eighth plague: locusts cover the earth, block out the sun
description_en: A locust swarm so dense it darkens the sky covers all of Egypt. At Moses's command the swarm is swept into the Red Sea.
research_notes: Reversed on command — not normal biological behaviour.

title_en: Ninth plague: total darkness for three days
description_en: A darkness that can be 'felt' covers Egypt for three days. Israelites have light in their dwellings. Egyptians cannot see one another or leave their homes.
research_notes: Tactile darkness ('felt'). Selective lighting — Israelites in Goshen have light. 72-hour duration. No natural explanation.

title_en: Tenth plague: death of the firstborn throughout Egypt
description_en: At midnight, all firstborn in Egypt die — from Pharaoh's son to prisoners. Israelite houses marked with lamb's blood are passed over. No Israelite firstborn dies.
research_notes: Precision targeting based on a biochemical marker (blood). The 'destroyer' (mashchit) in v.23 is an active agent, not a random event. Selective lethality.

title_en: Red Sea (Sea of Reeds) divided; walls of water
description_en: Moses stretches out his hand over the sea; a strong east wind blows all night and divides the water. Israelites cross on dry ground with walls of water on either side. Egyptians drown when Moses raises his hand again.
research_notes: Walls of water standing vertically. Egyptians' wheels removed (v.25). Pillar of fire/cloud involved (see BIB_OT_EXO_002). Von Däniken and Barry Downing analyse the mechanism.

title_en: Marah's bitter water made drinkable by a tree
description_en: YHWH shows Moses a piece of wood; Moses throws it into bitter water and it becomes sweet/drinkable.
research_notes: Chemical transformation via physical object. Object acts as a catalyst beyond its known properties.

title_en: Manna falls from heaven every morning in the wilderness
description_en: A flake-like substance appears on the ground every morning. It has properties: cannot be stored (rots overnight, except on the Sabbath); a double portion falls on the sixth day. Lasts 40 years.
research_notes: Programmatic delivery — 6 days + rest. Rule-based behaviour suggests intelligence. 40-year duration. Physical residue (jar kept in ark, Exo 16:33). Barry Downing discusses technological provision.

title_en: Water flows from rock at Rephidim
description_en: Moses strikes a rock at Horeb with his staff and water flows out for the congregation to drink.
research_notes: Physical object (staff) used as instrument. Cf. second incident at Zin (Num 20:7-11). Paul interprets the rock as a spiritual entity (1 Cor 10:4).

title_en: Nadab and Abihu consumed by divine fire
description_en: Nadab and Abihu offer 'unauthorised fire' before YHWH. Fire comes out from YHWH and consumes them. They die instantly inside the tabernacle.
research_notes: High-energy event inside a building. Immediate lethality. Cf. Elijah calling down fire (2 Kgs 1). No natural explanation for internal origin of fire.

title_en: Fire burns Taberah — divine consumption of the camp periphery
description_en: The people complain; fire from YHWH blazes among them and consumes some at the outskirts of the camp. Moses prays and the fire stops.
research_notes: Localised fire stops on command. Origin: 'from YHWH'. Place named Taberah ('burning').

title_en: Earth opens and swallows Korah, Dathan and Abiram; fire consumes 250
description_en: Ground splits open beneath the rebels and swallows them, their families and possessions. Simultaneously fire comes out and consumes the 250 men offering incense.
research_notes: Dual simultaneous event: sinkhole + fire. Precision targeting of specific individuals. Intact household engulfed. High UAP-relevance due to physical scale and precision.

title_en: Aaron's rod buds, blossoms and produces almonds overnight
description_en: Twelve staffs from tribal leaders are placed in the tent of meeting. Only Aaron's rod sprouts buds, produces blossoms, and bears ripe almonds — overnight.
research_notes: Accelerated biological process — full seasonal growth compressed to hours. Control group present (12 staffs). Kept as evidence in the ark (Heb 9:4).

title_en: Water from rock at Kadesh (Desert of Zin)
description_en: Moses strikes a rock twice and abundant water flows out for the community and livestock. Moses speaks instead of striking (as commanded) — a contrast with Exo 17.
research_notes: Repeated water-from-rock event. Cf. BIB_OT_NAT_015. Volume: enough for entire community and livestock.

title_en: Bronze serpent heals those bitten by fiery serpents
description_en: Fiery serpents kill many Israelites. YHWH instructs Moses to make a bronze serpent on a pole; anyone bitten who looks at it lives.
research_notes: Healing via visual contact with an object (not touch). Mechanism is non-local healing. Jesus cites this as a type of his own crucifixion (John 3:14). The bronze serpent (Nehushtan) later destroyed (2 Kgs 18:4).

title_en: Jordan River parts for the Israelites under Joshua
description_en: As the priests' feet touch the Jordan (at flood stage), the water stops flowing and stands in a heap far upstream. The people cross on dry ground.
research_notes: River stops at contact with ark-bearers' feet. Water 'stands in a heap' upstream (v.16). Second parting of water body (cf. Red Sea). Connected to the ark of the covenant as a physical instrument.

title_en: Walls of Jericho collapse after seven days of circling
description_ref: The Israelites march around Jericho once daily for six days, seven times on the seventh day, with seven priests blowing trumpets. At a long trumpet blast and a shout, the walls collapse outward.
description_en: The Israelites march around Jericho once daily for six days, seven times on the seventh day, with seven priests blowing trumpets. At a long trumpet blast and a shout, the walls collapse outward.
research_notes: Acoustic/ritual trigger for structural collapse. Archaeological evidence (Kathleen Kenyon, 1952) shows sudden wall collapse at Jericho. Rahab's house built into the wall survives (selective sparing).

title_en: Sun and moon stand still at Joshua's command
description_en: Joshua commands the sun and moon to stop. The sun stops in the middle of the sky for about a full day. 'The LORD fought for Israel.' Large hailstones also fall on the fleeing Amorites.
research_notes: Apparent alteration of Earth's rotation or orbital mechanics for ~24 hours. 'No day like it before or since' (v.14). Parallels Hezekiah's sun reversal (2 Kgs 20:9-11). Among the most dramatic physical anomalies in scripture.

title_en: Gideon's fleece: wet when ground is dry, dry when ground is wet
description_en: Gideon asks for a sign: wool fleece on the ground. First night: fleece soaked, ground dry. Second night: fleece dry, ground covered with dew. Both tests fulfilled.
research_notes: Reversal of natural moisture behaviour. Twice on request. Used as confirmation protocol before military action.

title_en: Samson's supernatural strength from the Spirit of YHWH
description_en: The Spirit of YHWH comes on Samson at various moments, granting exceptional physical strength: tearing a lion apart barehanded, killing 1000 men with a jawbone, carrying Gaza city gates.
research_notes: Spirit-induced physical augmentation. Episodes are distinct events. Strength lost when hair is cut (Jdg 16:17) — physical locus of power.

title_en: Ark of the Covenant causes plague on Philistines; tumours and rats
description_en: The ark is captured by Philistines and placed in Dagon's temple. Dagon's statue falls and breaks. The people of Ashdod, Gath, and Ekron are struck with tumours. 70 men of Bethshemesh die for looking inside the ark.
research_notes: Radiation-like effects: proximity to the ark causes disease and death. Statute toppled overnight by unseen force. 'Tumours' (or haemorrhoids, LXX: emerods) and rats suggest bubonic plague-like symptoms. Cf. Jones (1980): ark as electromagnetic device.

title_en: Thunder and rain in harvest season destroys Philistines
description_en: Samuel calls on YHWH and YHWH sends thunder and rain during wheat harvest (dry season). The Philistines are thrown into confusion and routed.
research_notes: Weather as a weapon, out-of-season. Cf. 1 Sam 12:18 (thunder and rain in another dry-season context).

title_en: Uzzah struck dead for touching the ark
description_en: While the ark is transported on a cart, the oxen stumble. Uzzah reaches out and steadies the ark. YHWH strikes him dead immediately.
research_notes: Immediate lethal response to physical contact with a sacred object. Suggests the ark had an active physical property (electromagnetic? radiation?). David's subsequent fear (v.9) indicates unpredictability.

title_en: Jeroboam's hand withers; altar cracks, ashes pour out
description_en: Jeroboam points at the prophet and orders his arrest. His hand withers and cannot be pulled back. The altar simultaneously splits and ashes pour from it. At the prophet's prayer, the king's hand is restored.
research_notes: Three simultaneous events: hand withers, altar cracks, ashes pour. Reversed on intercession. Instantaneous physical effect.

title_en: Elijah: widow of Zarephath's jar of flour and jug of oil never empty
description_en: Elijah tells a starving widow to bake for him first. Her jar of flour is not used up and her jug of oil does not run dry until the drought ends. Daily miraculous provision for months.
research_notes: Sustained matter multiplication. Daily replenishment without observable input. Similar to Jesus's feeding of the 5000.

title_en: Elijah raises the widow of Zarephath's son from death
description_en: The widow's son stops breathing. Elijah takes him to an upper room, stretches himself over the child three times, and prays. The child's life returns.
research_notes: First resurrection in the Bible. Physical ritual (body contact, three repetitions). Widow concludes: 'You are a man of God.' Pre-Christian resurrection precedent.

title_en: Fire from heaven consumes Elijah's sacrifice on Mount Carmel
description_en: Elijah's altar is drenched with water three times (12 jars). He prays and fire falls from YHWH and burns up the sacrifice, the altar stones, the soil, and the water in the trench.
research_notes: High-energy event: consumes stone, soil, and water. 850 witnesses (prophets of Baal and Asherah + Israel). After multiple failed calls by Baal prophets — controlled conditions. Cf. BIB_OT_NAT_016.

title_en: Elijah prays and the drought breaks; rain returns
description_en: After three and a half years of drought, Elijah prays seven times. A cloud the size of a man's hand rises from the sea; heavy rain falls.
research_notes: Weather control via prayer. Cf. James 5:17-18. 3.5-year drought bracketed by prophetic proclamation and prayer.

title_en: Elijah calls fire from heaven on two companies of soldiers
description_en: King Ahaziah sends a captain of fifty with his men to arrest Elijah. Elijah calls fire down from heaven; it consumes them. A second company of fifty is also consumed. The third captain begs for mercy and is spared.
research_notes: Directed energy weapon effect — twice, 50 men each time. Spared third group at Elijah's discretion. Cf. BIB_OT_NAT_033 and BIB_OT_NAT_016.

title_en: Elijah and Elisha cross the Jordan on dry ground; river divides
description_en: Elijah takes his cloak, strikes the water and it divides, and they cross. After Elijah's ascension, Elisha strikes the water with the same cloak and crosses back.
research_notes: River divides twice — once by Elijah, once by Elisha with same garment. Cloak as physical instrument. 50 prophets witness from a distance. Parallels Moses/Joshua Jordan crossings.

title_en: Elisha heals the waters of Jericho with salt
description_en: The people of Jericho report their water is bad and causing deaths. Elisha puts salt in a new bowl and throws it into the spring. The water is permanently purified.
research_notes: Permanent environmental remediation via small physical intervention (salt). Cf. Marah (BIB_OT_NAT_013) — wood into bitter water.

title_en: Elisha multiplies a widow's oil to pay off debt
description_en: A prophet's widow is destitute; creditors will take her sons. Elisha instructs her to collect empty jars from neighbours, pour her small flask of oil into them. The oil keeps flowing until all jars are full — then stops.
research_notes: Matter multiplication: oil stops precisely when no more jars are available. The capacity limit is set by available vessels, not the source. Cf. widow of Zarephath (BIB_OT_NAT_031).

title_en: Elisha raises the Shunammite woman's son from death
description_en: The Shunammite woman's son dies. Elisha lies on the child body-to-body, the child's body warms, he sneezes seven times and opens his eyes.
research_notes: Physical contact ritual (body stretched over body — same as Elijah in 1 Kgs 17). Reanimation with specific physical signs (warming, sneezing). Pre-Christian resurrection.

title_en: Elisha purifies poisonous stew with flour
description_en: Prophets accidentally add poisonous gourds to a stew. Elisha puts flour in the pot and the stew is harmless.
research_notes: Toxin neutralisation via added substance. Cf. Marah and Jericho water healings.

title_en: Elisha feeds 100 men with 20 loaves — with food to spare
description_en: Elisha commands that 20 loaves of barley and fresh grain be distributed to 100 men. His servant protests the insufficiency; Elisha says they will eat and have some left over. It happens.
research_notes: Food multiplication: 20 loaves for 100 people with surplus. Direct precedent for Jesus's feeding of the 5000.

title_en: Naaman's leprosy healed after seven washings in the Jordan
description_en: Syrian military commander Naaman has leprosy. Elisha's instructions: wash in the Jordan seven times. Naaman does so reluctantly; his skin becomes 'clean like a young child's'.
research_notes: Complete healing of incurable disease. Protocol-based: seven immersions (not six, not eight). Recipient is a foreign military officer — cross-cultural relevance. Gehazi's subsequent leprosy (2 Kgs 5:27) is the reverse judgment.

title_en: Gehazi struck with Naaman's leprosy as punishment
description_en: Elisha's servant Gehazi secretly takes silver and clothing from Naaman (after Elisha refused gifts). Elisha confronts him and declares Naaman's leprosy will cling to him forever.
research_notes: Instantaneous disease transfer. Elisha claims to have witnessed Gehazi's actions clairvoyantly (v.26). Reverse of Naaman's healing.

title_en: Iron axe head floats on the Jordan River
description_en: A prophet's iron axe head falls into the Jordan. Elisha cuts a stick, throws it in at the spot and the iron floats to the surface.
research_notes: Reversal of buoyancy for a dense metal object. Physical instrument (stick) used as catalyst. Economically motivated (axe was borrowed, v.5).

title_en: Syrian army struck blind, led to Samaria, then healed
description_en: Elisha prays that a Syrian army sent to capture him be struck with blindness. He leads them to Samaria. He prays their eyes be opened — they find themselves inside enemy territory.
research_notes: Induced blindness (and restoration) via prayer. Military deception using supernatural means. Cf. blinding of Sodomites (Gen 19:11) and Paul's Damascus road.

title_en: Dead man revived after touching Elisha's bones
description_en: A man's body is thrown into Elisha's tomb in a panic. As soon as it touches Elisha's bones, the man revives and stands up.
research_notes: Post-mortem residual power in physical remains. Contact-based resurrection (not prayer, not ritual). Unique case in scripture. Cf. woman healed by touching Jesus's garment (Mark 5:27).

title_en: Angel of the LORD destroys 185,000 Assyrian soldiers overnight
description_en: Hezekiah prays after Sennacherib's threatening letter. That night, the Angel of the LORD strikes 185,000 in the Assyrian camp. In the morning they are all dead.
research_notes: 185,000 deaths in a single night by an angel acting as a weapon. No battle, no visible combat. Herodotus (Hist. 2.141) independently records a mouse-borne plague at Pelusium that may refer to this event. Scale: largest single supernatural kill in scripture.

title_en: Shadow goes back ten steps on Hezekiah's sundial
description_en: As a sign of healing (see 2 Kgs 20:1-7), the shadow on the sundial moves backward ten steps. Isaiah asks which direction the sign should go — it goes backward.
research_notes: Apparent reversal of time/Earth rotation (or refraction anomaly). Accompanies healing of terminal illness. Cf. Joshua's sun standing still (BIB_OT_NAT_024). Both events involve apparent interference with solar mechanics.

title_en: Uzziah struck with leprosy for burning incense in the temple
description_en: King Uzziah (Azariah) attempts to burn incense in the temple, a priestly role. As priests confront him, leprosy breaks out on his forehead. He has leprosy until death.
research_notes: Instantaneous disease onset correlated with violation of a physical boundary (entering priestly space). Cf. Gehazi (BIB_OT_NAT_043) and Miriam (Num 12:10).

title_en: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego unharmed in the furnace; fourth figure
description_en: Three men thrown into a furnace heated seven times normal. They walk around unbound and unharmed. Nebuchadnezzar sees four figures, the fourth 'like a son of the gods'. They emerge with no burns, no smell of smoke.
research_notes: Fourth figure identified as angel or divine being. Zero physical evidence of fire (clothes, hair, skin, smell). Ropes burned; bodies and clothing intact. High UAP-relevance: entity appears inside extreme physical conditions.

title_en: Daniel in the lions' den; angel shuts the lions' mouths
description_en: Daniel is thrown into a den of lions after refusing to stop praying. He is unharmed. The king finds him alive and declares it was Daniel's God who sent his angel to shut the lions' mouths.
research_notes: Invisible angel controls predator behaviour. Zero injuries on Daniel. The accusers thrown in immediately are mauled before they hit the floor (v.24) — selective protection.

title_en: Jonah survives three days and nights inside a great fish
description_en: Jonah is thrown overboard and swallowed by a great fish. He remains alive inside for three days and three nights, prays, and is vomited onto dry land.
research_notes: Survival in hostile environment (zero oxygen, digestive acids). Three days/nights used by Jesus as sign of his own death/resurrection (Matt 12:40). The fish is 'appointed' by YHWH (v.17) — prepared/sent entity.

title_en: Jesus heals a leper with a touch
description_en: A man with leprosy kneels before Jesus. Jesus reaches out and touches him — against purity laws — saying 'Be clean'. The leprosy immediately leaves him.
research_notes: Instantaneous healing of incurable skin disease. Physical touch initiates healing — transgressing ritual boundary. Three independent accounts.

title_en: Jesus heals the centurion's servant at a distance
description_en: A Roman centurion's servant is paralysed and suffering. Jesus agrees to come but the centurion says a word from a distance is sufficient. Jesus heals at a distance; servant is well at that exact moment.
research_notes: Non-local healing: patient not present. Instantaneous at a distance. Military officer as witness. 'I have not found such great faith in Israel' — Jesus's highest commendation.

title_en: Jesus heals Peter's mother-in-law of a fever
description_en: Peter's mother-in-law is in bed with a high fever. Jesus touches her hand; the fever leaves immediately. She gets up and serves them.
research_notes: Luke adds that Jesus 'rebuked the fever' (personal speech to disease). Instantaneous recovery: she serves immediately.

title_en: Jesus heals the paralytic lowered through the roof
description_en: Four men lower a paralysed man through a roof to reach Jesus. Jesus first forgives sins, then heals the man, who picks up his mat and walks. Done publicly to demonstrate authority to forgive.
research_notes: Healing linked explicitly to sin-forgiveness — integrated physical-spiritual event. Large indoor crowd of witnesses including scribes (hostile).

title_en: Jesus heals a man's withered hand in a synagogue
description_en: A man with a shrivelled hand is in the synagogue on the Sabbath. Jesus tells him to stretch it out; the hand is completely restored.
research_notes: Instantaneous restoration of atrophied tissue. Performed in synagogue, observed by Pharisees (hostile witnesses). Triggers Pharisees' plot to kill Jesus (Mark 3:6).

title_en: Jesus heals the paralysed man at Bethesda pool
description_en: A man paralysed for 38 years lies at the pool of Bethesda. Jesus tells him: 'Get up, take your mat and walk.' He is immediately healed.
research_notes: 38 years of paralysis reversed instantly. Pool of Bethesda context: an angel stirring the water was believed to cause healing (John 5:4 — in some manuscripts). Jesus bypasses the protocol entirely.

title_en: Jesus heals the man born blind (clay + Siloam pool)
description_en: Jesus spits on the ground, makes clay, puts it on a blind man's eyes and tells him to wash in Siloam. He returns seeing. He has been blind since birth — no prior sight to 'restore'.
research_notes: Creation of a sensory system not previously present (congenital blindness). Two-step procedure involving physical substances (saliva, clay) and action (washing). Triggers extended investigation by Pharisees (John 9:13-41).

title_en: Jesus heals a deaf and mute man (fingers in ears, spittle)
description_en: Jesus takes the man aside privately, puts fingers in his ears, spits and touches his tongue, looks up to heaven with a sigh, says 'Ephphatha' (Be opened). The man's ears open and speech restored.
research_notes: Multi-step physical ritual (private, touch, spittle, Aramaic command). Specific verbal formula recorded ('Ephphatha'). Cf. BIB_NT_HEA_007 and BIB_NT_HEA_013 — Jesus uses physical substances in healing.

title_en: Jesus heals a blind man at Bethsaida in two stages
description_en: Jesus spits on the man's eyes, puts hands on him. The man sees people 'like trees walking'. Jesus places hands again; the man sees clearly. Only two-stage healing in the Gospels.
research_notes: Unique two-stage healing — partial effect before completion. Suggests a process or calibration. Taken away from the village (private). Only in Mark.

title_en: Jesus heals blind Bartimaeus (son of Timaeus)
description_en: Blind Bartimaeus calls out from the roadside at Jericho. Jesus stops, calls him, asks 'What do you want me to do for you?' Bartimaeus asks for sight; Jesus says 'Go, your faith has healed you.' Immediately he sees.
research_notes: Named recipient — unusual in miracle accounts. Healing attributed explicitly to faith rather than physical touch.

title_en: Jesus heals a woman bent double for 18 years
description_en: In a synagogue on the Sabbath, Jesus calls out a woman bent over and unable to straighten for 18 years. He puts his hands on her; she immediately straightens and praises God.
research_notes: Jesus calls the condition 'a spirit of infirmity' bound by Satan (v.11,16) — healing as deliverance. 18 years reversed instantly. Synagogue ruler protests Sabbath violation.

title_en: Jesus heals a man with dropsy (oedema) on the Sabbath
description_en: Jesus heals a man suffering from abnormal fluid accumulation (dropsy) at a Pharisee's house on the Sabbath. No details of the method given; immediate cure.
research_notes: Only occurrence of dropsy healing in scripture. Performed in front of Pharisees and lawyers (v.3). No recorded method of healing.

title_en: Jesus heals ten lepers at a distance; one returns
description_en: Ten lepers call out to Jesus from a distance. He tells them to show themselves to the priests. As they go, they are cleansed. Only one (a Samaritan) returns to give thanks.
research_notes: Non-local, delayed healing: 'as they went'. Mass healing (10 simultaneous). Cross-cultural: Samaritan recipient.

title_en: Jesus restores the high priest's servant's ear (Malchus)
description_en: In the Garden of Gethsemane, Peter cuts off the right ear of Malchus (the high priest's servant). Jesus touches the man's ear and heals it.
research_notes: Instant regrowth/reattachment of severed organ. Performed on an opponent (enemy combatant). Witness: arresting party. Only John names Malchus.

title_en: Jesus heals the royal official's son at a distance in Capernaum
description_en: A royal official's son is near death in Capernaum. Jesus (in Cana) says: 'Your son will live.' The man believes and leaves. His servants meet him: the fever broke at the exact hour Jesus spoke.
research_notes: Long-distance healing (~25 km). Timing confirmed independently by servants. Pure word-based healing (no touch, no physical contact). Second sign Jesus performs in Galilee.

title_en: Jesus casts out unclean spirit in the Capernaum synagogue
description_en: A man with an unclean spirit cries out in the synagogue. Jesus commands it to be silent and come out. The spirit convulses the man and comes out with a shriek.
research_notes: First recorded exorcism of Jesus. The spirit recognises Jesus as 'the Holy One of God' — knowledge anomaly. Physical effect: convulsion. Crowd reaction: amazement at new 'authority'.

title_en: Legion of demons cast out of the Gerasene man into swine
description_en: A naked man living among tombs has supernatural strength (chains could not hold him) and self-harms. Jesus commands the spirits out; they identify as 'Legion' (many). They beg to enter pigs; 2000 pigs rush into the lake and drown.
research_notes: Multiple entities (Legion = Roman regiment, ~6000). Demons negotiate destination. Physical evidence: 2000 pigs drown. Man restored to 'right mind', clothed, coherent. Most dramatic exorcism account in scripture.

title_en: Jesus casts demon from the Canaanite woman's daughter at a distance
description_en: A Canaanite woman begs Jesus to heal her daughter. Jesus heals her without being present. The mother returns home and finds the daughter lying in bed, the demon gone.
research_notes: Long-distance exorcism. Recipient not present. Cross-cultural: Canaanite/Syrophoenician (not Jewish). Woman's response (v.28) praised as 'great faith'.

title_en: Jesus casts out demon from boy with seizures
description_en: A boy has seizures, throws himself into fire and water. Disciples cannot cast it out. Jesus rebukes the spirit; it convulses the boy violently, then comes out. The boy appears dead. Jesus takes his hand and lifts him up.
research_notes: Disciples' prior failure establishes the entity's resistance. Boy appears dead after expulsion (near-death or healing crisis). Jesus explains disciples' failure: 'this kind comes out only by prayer' (Mark 9:29).

title_en: Jesus casts out blind and mute spirit
description_en: A demon-possessed man who was blind and mute is brought to Jesus. He casts out the demon; the man can see and speak. Pharisees attribute this to Beelzebub.
research_notes: Double cure (sight and speech) via exorcism. Triggers the Beelzebub controversy (Matt 12:24-32). Crowds: 'Could this be the Son of David?'

title_en: Seven demons cast out of Mary Magdalene
description_en: Mary Magdalene, described as a woman from whom seven demons had been cast out, becomes a core disciple and witness to the resurrection.
research_notes: Seven entities. Brief mention, no detailed account. Recipient becomes primary resurrection witness — transformation narrative. Mary is listed first among the women who followed Jesus.

title_en: Jesus turns water into wine at the wedding in Cana
description_en: Six stone jars (each holding 80-120 litres) filled with water become wine. The head waiter notes it is better than the wine already served.
research_notes: First public miracle ('sign') of Jesus. ~480-720 litres of wine. John calls it a 'sign' that revealed Jesus's glory. Molecular transformation: H2O into C2H5OH + complex organic compounds.

title_en: Jesus calms the storm with a command
description_en: A furious storm on the Sea of Galilee threatens to sink the boat. Jesus rebukes the wind and says 'Quiet! Be still!' The wind dies and it is completely calm.
research_notes: Instantaneous cessation of storm conditions (not gradual). Disciples: 'Even the wind and the waves obey him.' Jesus addresses the storm as a person — same command-form as exorcism.

title_en: Jesus feeds 5000 people with five loaves and two fish
description_en: 5000 men (plus women and children) fed from five barley loaves and two fish. Twelve baskets of leftovers collected. All eat and are satisfied.
research_notes: Only miracle recorded in all four gospels. Mass provision: >5000 persons. 12 baskets surplus. Direct parallel to Elisha's 100 men/20 loaves (BIB_OT_NAT_041). Triggers attempt to make Jesus king (John 6:15).

title_en: Jesus walks on water on the Sea of Galilee
description_en: Jesus walks to the disciples' boat across the water during a storm at night. Peter attempts the same, begins to sink, and is caught by Jesus. When they get in the boat, the wind stops.
research_notes: Apparent defiance of buoyancy and gravity. Peter replicates momentarily. Boat 'immediately' at the shore (John 6:21) — possible teleportation element. At night, in a storm.

title_en: Jesus feeds 4000 people with seven loaves and a few fish
description_en: In a remote place, 4000 men fed from seven loaves and a few small fish. Seven baskets of leftovers collected.
research_notes: Second mass feeding event. Different crowd, different location (possibly Gentile territory — Decapolis). Seven baskets surplus. Distinct from the feeding of 5000.

title_en: Jesus curses the fig tree; it withers by the next morning
description_en: Jesus finds a fig tree with leaves but no fruit and curses it. By morning the tree has withered from the roots.
research_notes: Directed desiccation of a living plant overnight, from roots up. Anomalous: instant biological death propagating from root to leaf. Used to illustrate faith and prayer.

title_en: Peter finds a coin in a fish's mouth to pay the temple tax
description_en: Jesus instructs Peter to cast a line into the lake; the first fish he catches will have a four-drachma coin in its mouth to pay the temple tax for both of them.
research_notes: Foreknowledge + miraculous provision (coin in specific fish, first catch). Tax exacty covers both Jesus and Peter. No human placed the coin. Only in Matthew.

title_en: Miraculous catch of fish — the calling of the first disciples
description_en: Simon and partners have fished all night and caught nothing. Jesus tells them to let down nets in deep water. They catch so many fish the nets begin to break and both boats begin to sink.
research_notes: Foreknowledge of fish location. Dramatic quantity. Simon Peter's reaction: prostrates himself before Jesus. Leads to immediate abandonment of livelihood.

title_en: Post-resurrection catch of 153 fish; Jesus on the shore
description_en: Disciples have caught nothing all night. The risen Jesus (not yet recognised) tells them to cast the net on the right side. 153 large fish caught; the net does not break.
research_notes: Specific number (153) — only precise count in any miracle account. Cf. BIB_NT_NAT_008 (same type of event, brackets Jesus's ministry). Net intact despite weight.

title_en: Jesus raises the daughter of Jairus from death
description_en: Jairus's twelve-year-old daughter dies while Jesus is delayed. Jesus enters the house and says she is sleeping, is laughed at. He takes her hand and says 'Talitha koum' (Little girl, get up). She rises immediately.
research_notes: Aramaic command formula recorded (Talitha koum). Three witnesses (Peter, James, John + parents). Declared dead by mourners. Immediate full restoration ('told them to give her something to eat').

title_en: Jesus raises the widow's son at Nain
description_en: Jesus encounters a funeral procession in Nain. A widow's only son is being carried out for burial. Jesus touches the bier (coffin carrier), tells the young man to get up. He sits up and speaks.
research_notes: Unsolicited resurrection — no request made. Jesus stops the funeral without being asked. Large crowd witnesses. Immediate response: 'A great prophet has appeared'; 'God has come to help his people' (v.16).

title_en: Jesus raises Lazarus after four days in the tomb
description_en: Lazarus has been in the tomb for four days. Jesus commands the stone removed (despite odour), prays, and shouts 'Lazarus, come out!' The dead man comes out still wrapped in burial cloths.
research_notes: Four days dead — beyond cultural threshold of 'three days' (soul believed to hover). Physical decomposition expected (v.39). Large crowd of witnesses (Jewish leaders, disciples, mourners). Directly triggers the Sanhedrin's decision to kill Jesus (John 11:53). Most dramatic resurrection in scripture.

title_en: Transfiguration of Jesus on the mountain
description_en: Jesus's face shines like the sun; his clothes become white as light. Moses and Elijah appear and talk with him. A bright cloud envelops them; a voice from the cloud says 'This is my Son.' Disciples fall on their faces.
research_notes: Three elements: physical luminous transformation, appearance of two deceased persons (Moses ~1400 BC, Elijah ~850 BC), voice from a cloud. Three witnesses (Peter, James, John). Cloud envelops them (CE4-adjacent). Moses's shining face has a precedent (BIB_OT_EXO_004).

title_en: Peter heals a man lame from birth at the Beautiful Gate
description_en: A man lame since birth begs at the temple gate. Peter says 'Silver or gold I do not have, but what I do have I give you — in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk.' He takes the man's hand; ankles immediately strengthen. He walks, jumps, praises God.
research_notes: Congenital lameness reversed (40+ years old, v.22). Physical contact (hand). Crowds gather; triggers Peter's sermon and arrest (Acts 4). 5000 believe.

title_en: Ananias and Sapphira struck dead for lying to the Holy Spirit
description_en: Ananias lies about the amount he received for land. Peter confronts him and he falls dead. Three hours later his wife Sapphira also lies; falls dead. Great fear comes on the church.
research_notes: Two independent sudden deaths, three hours apart, following verbal confrontation. No physical mechanism. Peter demonstrates foreknowledge of events (v.4,9). Closest NT parallel to Uzzah (BIB_OT_NAT_029) and Gehazi (BIB_OT_NAT_043).

title_en: Peter's shadow heals the sick in Jerusalem streets
description_en: People bring the sick into the streets and lay them on cots and mats so that Peter's shadow might fall on them as he passes by. All are healed.
research_notes: Non-contact healing via shadow (photon occlusion). Mass healing. Cf. woman healed by touching Jesus's garment (Mark 5:27-30) and Paul's handkerchiefs (Acts 19:11-12). Three distinct mechanisms of contact-free healing in the NT.

title_en: Philip teleported from Gaza road to Azotus
description_en: Philip baptises the Ethiopian eunuch. When they come up from the water, 'the Spirit of the Lord suddenly took Philip away, and the eunuch did not see him again'. Philip appears at Azotus (~30 km north) and continues preaching.
research_notes: Instantaneous physical translocation ~30 km. 'Suddenly taken away' — no transition. Directly witnessed absence by the eunuch. Only NT teleportation account. Cf. Ezekiel carried by the Spirit (Eze 3:12,14; 8:3; 11:1) and Elijah's reputation for being transported (1 Kgs 18:12).

title_en: Paul heals a man lame from birth at Lystra
description_en: Paul notices a man lame from birth listening to him. Paul looks at him and says 'Stand up on your feet!' The man jumps up and walks.
research_notes: Congenital lameness (never walked). Verbal command only — no touch. Crowd interprets Paul and Barnabas as Hermes and Zeus descended (v.11-12). Parallel to Peter's healing at the Beautiful Gate (BIB_NT_APO_001).

title_en: Paul casts out a spirit of divination from a slave girl
description_en: A slave girl with a 'spirit of Python' follows Paul for days, proclaiming him. Paul turns and commands the spirit out in Jesus's name. It leaves immediately. Her owners, losing profit, have Paul arrested.
research_notes: Spirit of divination: economic value as fortune-teller. Instantaneous at command. Removal verified by loss of economic function. Triggers Paul's arrest and imprisonment.

title_en: Earthquake opens prison doors and unfastens chains — Paul and Silas
description_en: Paul and Silas pray and sing hymns at midnight in prison. A violent earthquake shakes the foundations. All doors open and all chains come loose. The jailer, fearing prisoners escaped, is about to kill himself; Paul stops him.
research_notes: Prayer-triggered seismic event of precise effect: ALL doors open simultaneously, ALL chains loose. No prisoner escapes (they remain — anomalous choice). Jailer converts.

title_en: Paul raises Eutychus after fall from third-floor window
description_en: Eutychus falls asleep during Paul's sermon and falls from a third-floor window. He is picked up dead. Paul goes down, throws himself on the young man and embraces him: 'He's alive.' He recovers fully.
research_notes: Death by impact (three-floor fall) reversed by physical contact and embrace. Cf. Elijah/Elisha body-contact resurrection method (BIB_OT_NAT_032, BIB_OT_NAT_039). Witnesses: gathered church. 'Taken home alive' — full recovery.

title_en: Elymas the sorcerer struck blind by Paul
description_en: Bar-Jesus (Elymas), a sorcerer and false prophet, opposes Paul before the proconsul Sergius Paulus. Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, says: 'You will be blind.' Immediately mist and darkness comes over Elymas.
research_notes: Directed blindness as judicial act. Cf. Syrian army blinded by Elisha (BIB_OT_NAT_045) and Paul's own blindness on Damascus road. Witnesses: proconsul and attendants. Proconsul converts.

title_en: Paul unharmed by viper bite on Malta
description_en: On Malta after a shipwreck, Paul gathers firewood. A viper fastens onto his hand. The islanders expect him to swell and fall dead. Nothing happens. They conclude he is a god.
research_notes: Venom immunity (or snake's venom neutralised). Cf. Mark 16:18 ('pick up snakes with their hands and not be hurt'). Indigenous witnesses (Maltese) with baseline expectation of death. No physical symptoms.

title_en: Paul heals Publius's father of fever and dysentery
description_en: On Malta, the chief official's father lies ill with fever and dysentery. Paul goes in, prays, lays hands on him and heals him. After this all sick on the island come and are healed.
research_notes: Specific diagnosis (fever + dysentery). Physical contact (laying on hands). Mass healing of island population follows. Triggers gift-giving from Maltese (v.10).

title_en: Peter raises Dorcas (Tabitha) from death
description_en: Dorcas, a disciple known for good works, dies. Peter is sent for. He clears the room, kneels and prays, then turns to her body and says 'Tabitha, get up.' She opens her eyes, and Peter helps her to her feet.
research_notes: Aramaic command formula (Tabitha, koum — cf. Talitha koum in BIB_NT_RES_001). Same private room protocol as Elijah/Elisha. Many believe as a result. Joppa locale.

title_en: Peter heals Aeneas, paralysed for eight years
description_en: Peter finds Aeneas bedridden for eight years with paralysis. Peter says: 'Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and roll up your mat.' Immediately Aeneas gets up. All who see him in the region turn to the Lord.
research_notes: Eight years of paralysis reversed instantly. Regional mass conversion follows single healing event. Lyda and Sharon regions affected.

title_en: Paul's handkerchiefs and aprons heal the sick and exorcise demons
description_en: Handkerchiefs and aprons that have touched Paul are taken to the sick. Their illnesses are cured and evil spirits leave them.
research_notes: Object-mediated healing (physical items retain/transfer healing property). Cf. Peter's shadow (BIB_NT_APO_003) and Elisha's bones (BIB_OT_NAT_046). Three distinct mechanisms of residual-physical healing in scripture.

title_en: Peter freed from prison by an angel; passes iron gate that opens by itself
description_en: Peter is in prison, chained between two soldiers. An angel appears, light fills the cell, chains fall off. The angel leads him through two guard posts and an iron gate that opens by itself. Peter thinks it is a vision; realises it is real outside.
research_notes: Angel with light emission, undetected by guards, chain removal, gate opens automatically. Peter believes it is a vision until outside — subjective reality confusion. Cf. Acts 5:17-25 (earlier apostles' prison escape). The angel 'leaves suddenly' (v.10) — disappears.
